reviews.text: GODBREAKERS is a fast and fluid action-roguelike. It adds a fun mechanic to the genre, called "Godbreaking", that lets you absorb and use the abilities of enemies - but only once! The combat is quick, with simple combos and dashes that can cancel skills. We enjoyed the boss designs, as all of them have their own patterns and mechanics; the only thing all of them have in common are add spawns, which can be annoying, but are required for Godbreaking. Its strong-suit is the co-op for up to 4 players. You can share items, resurrect and support each other - and it's overall a lot of fun to play as a team. What holds it back a bit is the amount of content and variation for the runs. It has 6 biomes in total and one run ("cycle") means clearing four of them. The biomes offer some variation in the rooms, but the miniboss and boss are always the same. After clearing your first full run, you unlock "Tangles", difficulty modifiers of which you can apply up to 5 at once. Those unlock more head, weapon and body skins, if you clear them successfully. We would love to see more content added in the future! [i]We received keys from the developers to review the game ahead of launch, but this review is not sponsored.[/i] If you're curious to see and hear more, we made a video review from a duo perspective: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IyOn4CN_l1c

I cautiously recommend this game. The Good: -The combat is fast, fluid and you can cancel out of almost anything with a dash. -The Buildcrafting is generally good, a bit underwhelming, but there's enough to keep each run fresh and it's fun to stack damage over time effects. -Stealing skills from enemies and using them is a good mechanic that adds variety to combat. -Most boss fights have good design. -The story has lot's of interesting lore. The Bad: -Hard to play solo, No hit stun, and not a lot of defensive options, so get used to running around and dodging all the time. -The Poison planet boss is terrible. -Whiny NPC's. Full Video Review on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MBLodAyPjOI

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44181848/] 【更多适合Steam Deck的好游戏推荐，请关注GPD掌机鉴赏家！】[/url] 在独立游戏领域，以“弑神”为主题的作品并不少见，但《破神者》通过其独特的“力量吸收”机制和流畅的战斗系统，为这一题材注入了新鲜血液。这款由To The Sky开发、Thunderless Publishing发行的合作砍杀动作游戏，试图在roguelike框架下打造出兼具技巧与策略的战斗体验。经过初步的体验，我认为它已经展现出了显著的潜力。 战斗体验：行云流水但缺乏重量感 《破神者》最突出的亮点在于其高速流畅的战斗系统。游戏实现了攻击、冲刺与技能的无缝衔接，特别是“取消动作”机制让连招更加自由。你可以在一套连击中途突然取消后摇，转而闪避或释放技能，这种设计极大地提升了战斗的流畅度和操作上限。 核心的“破神一击”机制——通过削弱敌人并吸收其技能反过来对付他们——确实是游戏的亮点。当BOSS战进入关键阶段，成功夺取敌人力量并释放毁灭性反击的体验令人满足。 不过，游戏在打击感方面存在明显不足。武器命中反馈薄弱，缺乏应有的冲击力，这降低了战斗的爽快感。更奇怪的是，敌人似乎没有硬直机制，即使承受重击也会继续攻击，这迫使玩家不得不采取更保守的“打带跑”策略。 roguelike元素：设计保守，构建深度不足 作为一款roguelike游戏，《破神者》目前的构筑多样性相对有限。游戏提供了六种不同的原型角色，每种都有独特的武器和特质，玩家可以通过解锁新武器和技能来扩展选择。 但问题在于，游戏中获得的增益和技能组合缺乏协同效应，难以形成真正改变游戏玩法的强大构建。玩家很少能体验到传统roguelike游戏中那种通过巧妙组合产生质变的快感。游戏的roguelike元素感觉更像是对趋势的妥协，而非经过深思熟虑的核心设计。 合作体验：欢乐但不够完善 《破神者》支持1-4人在线合作，这是游戏的主要卖点之一。与朋友一起挑战各种奇异生态环境中的残暴头目，协调技能、连携攻击确实能带来单人游戏无法比拟的乐趣。 然而，游戏目前缺乏匹配系统或大厅功能，寻找队友只能通过外部渠道。虽然开发者可能希望玩家主要与朋友组队，但这无疑限制了游戏的可玩性和可及性。 BOSS设计：亮点与挑战并存 游戏中的头目战设计是另一大亮点。这些拥有多阶段战斗的BOSS各具特色，攻击模式多变且个性鲜明。它们的技能提示清晰，动画抬手明显，让玩家能够通过观察和反应来应对，而非依赖单纯的数值碾压。 但正如试玩反馈所指出的，生命药水系统可能过于严苛。药水获取有限，使用时有漫长硬直，且在不同区域间不会自动补充，这给新手玩家带来了不小的挫折感。 视听表现与世界观 游戏跨越六个独特的生物群落，每个都有独特的敌人和挑战。这些环境设计充满想象力，配合游戏背景设定——在一个人类已被AI抹除的世界里，作为女巫团最后武器战斗——构建了一个引人入胜的科幻世界观。 不过，当前版本的本地化质量有待提高。机翻痕迹明显的文本虽然不影响基本理解，但确实削弱了剧情的沉浸感。 总结：值得一试的潜力之作 《破神者》呈现了一个坚实的核心战斗系统，特别是其取消动作和力量吸收机制为合作动作游戏带来了新鲜感。然而，roguelike元素的浅薄和某些反直觉的设计选择阻碍了它成为一款出色的游戏。 优势： 流畅高速的战斗系统，取消动作机制增加操作上限 创新的“破神一击”技能吸收机制 设计精良的多阶段BOSS战 支持1-4人合作，适合好友联机 不足： 武器打击感薄弱，敌人缺乏硬直 Roguelike元素深度不足，构建多样性有限 无匹配系统，合作体验受限 生命药水系统过于严苛

It is ok, and starts out really fun. Then it just kind of falls apart. Combat just turns into you dodging 80% of the time, because enemy attack patterns don't seem to match player ability. You have a heavy attack and a charged heavy attack, but there is almost no time to ever use them. Then when you do the damage is pretty much the same as a few light attacks. Bosses are extremely easy, and only ever difficult when they spawn extra normal enemies. The bosses have cool attacks and well telegraphed patterns, which could be made harder rather easily. And having "adds" on every boss just to make them somewhat challenging is really silly. Items and upgrades are ok, and there are some neat synergies. They were inspired by Risk of Rain 2, but they really should have followed it closer if they wanted that same fun factor. Literally just a "melee" Risk of Rain 2 with the combat from Godbreakers would amazing. Instead we have just a series of rooms with enemies over and over, and extremely limited equipment slots.

A friend recommended GODBREAKERS to me just as a fun game we could play, which we did after playing the demo. Finally, after 10 hours, and getting the true ending, I wanted to post a review to help people who might be into the same tastes as me decide if this game is worth it. I'm no rogue-like/lite hyper gamer, but I have played quite a few, and enjoy the genre as well as the tough challenges they often offer, if that helps. [h1]GODBREAKERS[/h1] is a 3D-action roguelite where you play as a... creature? Not sure, but you play a humanoid thing who is brought forth by three strange beings collectively called the Coven. Your goal is to stop a rampant AI called the [b]Monad[/b] from destroying the sun, and to do so will mean you need to fight through his cronies called the Hylerians (I know I'm spelling that wrong probably...), travel through their worlds, and put a stop to Monad once and for all. Starting with the positive... [h3]the core gameplay and combat of GODBREAKERS is excellent and solid.[/h3] It's style of combat is more slow, intentional, and grounded. Enemies don't get hitstun, your dodge doesn't have I-frames, and your attacks are slower than games like DmC or Ninja Gaiden. But that's not a negative thing IMO. The controls are tight and hitting things is still satisfying. In-short, you have access to a Primary Attack (Light Attack), a Secondary Attack (Heavy Attack), a Charge Attack and a Combo Attack. Unique to GODBREAKERS is it's Godbreak mechanic, where you can execute enemies with low enough health, stealing a one-time use ability from them. It's fun to Godbreak new enemies and see what abilities they give you, and a welcome addition to keep combat interesting. The game also offers six Archetypes (basically weapons) to play with. Each one has their own unique weapon ability, passive, attack animations, and changes your health. Alongside this, each weapon has 3 unique abilities you can select from, though the other two options must be unlocked by completing certain challenges. All of this solidify the combat as this game's best aspect. If there's anything else I want to say is stand-out... [h3]the soundtrack[/h3] is amazing. A mix of orchestral, rock, and electronic, each song keeps combat energetic, lively, and is overall a banger to listen to. The boss music is by far the stand-out here, and it's one of the reasons I like fighting each boss. Whoever composed the soundtrack did an amazing job, and I'm glad the soundtrack is available for purchase so I can support the devs in this aspect. And on the list of things I would like to add into the positives... [h3]the artstyle and aesthetic[/h3] is a weird one that I didn't expect I'd like as much as I did. Everything has this weird abstract aura to it when it comes to the artstyle, from the enemies, bosses, to the worldbuilding itself, but I learned to enjoy it as I played through. Not only that, but each biome is diverse in aesthetic, from the desert plains of Uhr, the gardens of Astaphane and even the... the weirdness of Karaja, so there's always something catching your eye. It helps alot that this game feels like a cartoon with how things are animated. Hard hits splat you on the ground, and enemies move with the sudden-ness that feels slapstick. It's overall fun, and feels as though alot of care was put into it. But for all that's good, there are some serious flaws that destroy the experience for me and made me reconsider if this game was worth it's asking price. And the biggest of all are it's roguelite elements. [h2]Out of all the roguelite games I've played, GODBREAKERS's in-run progression, upgrades, and meta-progression are some of the most boring I've played, to the point where it makes me wonder why they even bothered making this game a roguelite.[/h2] The extent of your in-run progression lies in [b]Essence and Fragments.[/b] Essence are basically tiny stat-boosts that you can acquire over the course of your run, and when I say tiny, I do mean tiny. We're talking, "1% extra chance to inflict a DoT with attacks," and "1% bonus critical chance." They're so small that it doesn't feel like they matter, nor do they make me feel stronger. It's made even worse as you cannot convert essences you don't need, instead only able to recycle them into currency so you can hopefully buy the right ones in randomized shops. At most, you'll probably be able to stack 10 to 15 of one kind in a single run. It's boring and completely unexciting. Fragments are armor pieces you can equip on your person. A cool thing about Fragments is that they actually appear on your character when you equip them, which makes getting one actually kinda fun. But just like Essences, the effects they give are conditional and not very exciting. Stuff like "Dash Attacks have 35% bonus crit chance," or "Combo Attacks have a 25% to inflict a debuff." Almost all the roguelite progression in a run gives such small and trivial effects, when roguelites are fun when there's a real sense of build progression, and seeing a build come online and empower your strengths and weaknesses, maybe even encouraging a change in playstyle. [h2]But GODBREAKERS has none of those feelings, and by the time I end a run, I can only really wish that the upgrades were just more meaningful to pick up.[/h2] Echoes are much of the same, acting as this game's meta-progression, but just like Essences and Fragments, they too feel boring to unlock. [h2]Without strong roguelite elements to keep me coming back for more, the game's second biggest short-coming is on display: a concerning lack of content.[/h2] There are 6 unique biomes, but runs consist of 4 different levels, and the 4th level is just a boss battle with no traversal in-between. Once you clear the game and experience all 6 biomes... That's it. And normally for a roguelite, that wouldn't be so bad, as these games are meant to be replayable, but without the strong roguelite elements, it just feels hollow. There are challenges and cosmetics, and but nothing that encourages me to play again. There are Tangles, which are difficulty modifiers you can activate, and I did replay the game to try them out and have fun, but they suffer from a strange design decision: [b]you get no extra rewards aside from a one-time reward.[/b] I enjoy a good challenge, but also know most players want something else alongside that to make harder difficulties more enticing, so the game not offering extra rewards for activating Tangles is strange when every other roguelite I've played gives stuff like more meta-progression rewards or more resources in a run. Finally, the story... This game's story is boring, that's expected for a roguelite, but I think it's no excuse. The short runs and lack of content kill any sort of theme it may build, which in this case is about regaining your humanity. In order to get the true ending, you must complete story-specific quests where each boss will request you complete certain tasks when you're on their world. Doing all of their quests unlocks their unique Tangle, and you need to unlock all five to unlock the true ending. These quests are just boring tasks you'd find in a daily task list in something like a gacha game. Stuff like, "Hit 5 enemies with air attacks, Inflict this debuff 5 times, kill 5 enemies with the environment." These never felt like major reasons to replay the game, and the ending reward you get is a slightly different ending cutscene. What a letdown... [h2]To conclude my thoughts...[/h2] ...I was impressed with the demo, but quickly found that it was a whole third of the full release. This game just feels like it's still in Early Access, and while I do know the devs will add more content, it doesn't excuse the $27.99 asking price for how little it offers as a roguelite and as a complete game. I hope this game does well, and hope the devs turn this game into something worth it's price, because it has alot of potential. But for now, buy at your own discretion.

一句话概括：没有肉鸽构筑的乐趣，也没有动作游戏的爽感。不推荐。 1.所有敌人都有霸体，对上多个敌人时难找到出手机会，啥时候该闪避也不好看清，打得非常憋屈。 2.各种数值投放都挺抠门，肉鸽该有的构筑也不多，一局打下来感觉没什么成长。 ——因为能装备的位置就那么几个，当好不容易找到一个新装备，有不小的概率部位重复需要替换，如果是参考哈迪斯的设计，至少应该是有品质提升的。 ——本游戏构筑的核心思路我感觉是这样，先随便凑一套，获取足够的钱之后在商店刷一套不错的build（装备升级提升很大）。但是钱给的太少了... 3.太容易被摸掉血了，给的回复手段也不多。感觉是给拆到技能树里了，但我很难说这是个好设计。 4.吸取敌人技能的设定其实挺有意思的，但是感觉不够爽，除非多给我释放的机会（某个装备能高频释放吸收技） 5.索敌是个大问题，无论近战还是远程，都很容易打空！ 6.每个角色都有多种不同的攻击模组，但是这个没有和肉鸽结合起来，体验上感觉怎么打都大差不差

[h2] 破神者，出击！[/h2] 将敌人的能力变成我们自己的能力，这种感觉真的太酷啦!《GODBREAKERS》是一款非常有意思的多人联机PVE游戏，在这里我们将会前往各种奇妙的星球之间，在里面击杀怪物进行升级，从而继续挑战更强大的精英boss，体验多样化肉鸽元素，看看怎样谁才是真正的破神者。 游戏采用了偏向闯关的地图机制，我们要选择想要进入的星球，之后就要在其中不断地闯过各种关卡，抵达这个星球最终的boss房，将其击杀代表着成功征服这个星球。游戏在其中还设计了许多其他的NPC在其中，我们可以将击杀怪物所获得的资源来进行购买与强化，提升自身实力的同时也是一种成长的快乐。 [h2] 拳脚功夫肯定得到位[/h2] 感受行云流水一般的战斗，就如同德芙一般丝滑。游戏在战斗部分花了很多心思，翻滚跳跃，钩索牵引，各种各样的武器装备，让我们体验不同战斗所带来的快乐，每把武器都有着专属的武器技能，这可以很好地搭配武器原本的战斗方式，并且游戏体验变得富有特色。 像是支柱这个武器，如同它的名字一样，本体就像是一根巨大的柱子，我们的所有战斗动作都是大开大合充满了力量感，并且也因为武器的原因，整体的战斗动作是比较慢的，这在面对一些攻速较快的敌人时是一个比较致命的问题，而武器的技能就很好地填补了这个空缺，技能可以给自身构造出一道防护的屏障，在有效地抵挡住敌人的同时，还可以对近距离的敌人造成一定的伤害，这样武器的整体有了较为平衡的强度，手感以及上手难度也不会过于复杂。 游戏对其他武器也类似的调整，甚至当我们游玩得足够深入以后，我们还会解锁同武器的不同武器技能，个性化的搭配走出我们自己的战斗流派。 [h2] 你的技能将为我所用[/h2] 除了武器的不同，游戏还加入了最有特点的吸收机制，虽然游戏拥有类似肉鸽的遗物机制，可以将探索过程中的所掉落的效果道具，直接安装在自己身上激活其内部存在的效果。但让我感觉最有意思的还是吸收机制，我们在战斗的时候可以注意右下角的一个蓄能槽在不断地增加。一旦到满就意味着我们可以使用吸收技能，像是一般的怪物处于低血量时就可以使用，将其杀死的同时，把原本拥有的能力从身上剥离出来。这样我们就能使用一次它的能力，根据我们吸收的怪物不同，获得的能力也不同。并且在吸收的时候我们将处于无敌状态，也可以通过这个能力去规避一些攻击，这让战斗环节又增色了不少。 并且游戏在画面方面表现也很不错，类似战斗时候角色对应的动作所展现打击感，特别是星球之中场景的设计，每颗星球都有自己的特色，无论是怪物还是场景。我们会因为误触地图上的机关而变得小心，也会因为面对怪堆的多样攻击时来回不停地到处闪躲，体验星球之间不一样的魅力。 [h2] 总结[/h2] 整体来说本作的水平还是较为不错的，画面表现以及战斗手感方面都有在认真制作，目前主要的问题是内容上还是有点太少了，玩起来不够尽兴，但确实上头停不下来。感觉值得要注意的一点是本作的怪物基本不吃控制和僵直，这会使得在战斗的时候都只能通过利用攻击间隙来偷刀，这是比较难受的地方，而且丧失了很多连招的可能，希望制作组之后可以在调整一下，感觉本作的潜力还是很大的。 [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]

Its biggest flaw is the lack of enemy stagger implementation—even a heavy-hitting attack cannot interrupt the attack wind-up of the weakest foes, reducing this action game to a turn-based style of gameplay where you attack once and dodge once. As for the roguelike elements, the build crafting is actually quite well-executed and not as bad as some reviews claim. With the right shard selections, you can still achieve high-damage clears and one-shot bosses. Further refinements in this aspect would be welcome. Your top priority right now should be enabling players to interrupt the attack wind-up of minor enemies, as well as ensuring that heavy-hitting attacks can stagger all non-boss enemies. In one of the challenges under the Recollections Mode from the latest update, I unleashed screen-filling explosive damage, yet the enemies kept attacking unaffected. So after completing all achievements in this game I can start to understand why it only has 73% positive reviews. I do love the loop of this game and the gameplay mechanics that are unique such as the absorption. However for a roguelike it's incredibly shallow. Whereas the loop is enjoyable I found it hard to be constantly challenged in this game, when I feel that being challenged is one of the most important parts or roguelike games, as the whole idea is to build up your knowledge overtime so that the combat feels more rewarding for the player. However in this game, despite the diversity of enemies, I found that you can literally deal with every enemy by dodging and it ends up making the combat feel too repetitive too quickly. Now there are some ways to directly challenge the player and make their ability to dodge and evade such through the Tangles. However I find even with the Tangle that makes you have one less dodge paired with the Tangle that makes you stumble on stamina depletion doesn't make it challenging enough. So unfortunately the games dependence on the Tangles to further increase difficulty just doesn't do it for me, and clearly a lot of people feel that way as well. This shouldn't be taken as a completely negative review, I did really enjoy this game otherwise I wouldn't have done all of the achievements, but unfortunately I don't think it's something I would ever revisit unless some serious gameplay shifts happen. And due to the low replay ability, this game is definitely not worth it's full price. So if it comes on offer and you're a roguelike fan then maybe give it a go.

GODBREAKERS is a high-energy action roguelite that leans unapologetically into spectacle, speed, and power fantasy, delivering an experience that prioritizes momentum and aggression over careful restraint. Developed by To The Sky and published by Thunderful Publishing, the game presents a sci-fi setting where humanity has already fallen, wiped out by a runaway artificial intelligence, and the last hope lies in resurrected warriors known as Godbreakers. Rather than dwelling heavily on exposition, the game quickly establishes its premise and throws players into combat, making it clear that its primary focus is the thrill of battle and the joy of mastering its systems. Combat is the defining feature of GODBREAKERS, and it is designed to feel fast, fluid, and relentlessly forward-moving. Players dash, strike, and chain attacks together with minimal downtime, encouraged to stay on the offensive at all times. Central to this is the Godbreak mechanic, which allows players to weaken enemies and absorb their abilities mid-fight, turning foes into temporary sources of power. This creates a dynamic flow where battles constantly evolve, as each absorbed ability can dramatically alter how the next encounter unfolds. Rather than committing to a rigid build from the start, players are incentivized to adapt on the fly, making moment-to-moment decision-making just as important as long-term planning. The roguelite structure supports this flexibility by framing each run as a self-contained experiment. Levels are arranged across a series of distinct biomes, each with its own visual identity, enemy behaviors, and environmental challenges. As players progress, enemy density and complexity increase, demanding sharper reflexes and better understanding of combat mechanics. Boss encounters punctuate these runs, serving as endurance tests that push players to fully exploit mobility, positioning, and absorbed powers. While the overall structure is familiar to genre fans, the emphasis on chaining abilities and aggressive play gives each run a unique rhythm. Progression outside of individual runs provides a steady sense of growth without undermining the game’s emphasis on skill. Unlockable archetypes, abilities, and modifiers expand the range of possible playstyles, allowing players to experiment with different approaches to combat. Some builds favor raw damage and speed, while others emphasize control, survivability, or synergy between absorbed abilities. This progression helps maintain motivation across repeated runs, even when failure is frequent, as each attempt contributes to a broader sense of mastery and customization. Cooperative play is a major strength of GODBREAKERS, supporting up to four players and amplifying the game’s chaotic energy. In co-op, combat becomes louder, faster, and more unpredictable, with multiple Godbreakers chaining abilities simultaneously and overwhelming enemies through sheer force and coordination. Team composition and timing begin to matter more, as overlapping abilities can either create devastating synergies or clutter the battlefield if poorly coordinated. While the game remains fully playable solo, the co-op mode highlights its design strengths most clearly, turning each run into a shared spectacle of destruction. Visually, the game adopts a bold, stylized look that complements its frenetic pace. Environments are vibrant and otherworldly, with exaggerated effects that make every dash, strike, and absorbed ability feel impactful. Enemy designs are striking and readable, ensuring that even in chaotic encounters, players can quickly identify threats. The audio design reinforces this intensity, with heavy sound effects and driving music that keep adrenaline high throughout a run. Performance is generally smooth, supporting the rapid movement and precise timing the combat demands. That said, GODBREAKERS does show some limitations over extended play. While the core mechanics are strong, the overall pool of biomes, enemies, and bosses is relatively modest, which can lead to a sense of repetition for players seeking long-term variety. Some encounters can feel overly durable, slowing the pace and diminishing the otherwise sharp combat flow. Additionally, while progression systems are satisfying, they may lack the depth and long-term complexity found in genre leaders, making the game feel more immediately exciting than endlessly deep. Ultimately, GODBREAKERS succeeds by delivering exactly what it promises: fast, aggressive action built around stylish combat and flexible power systems. It may not redefine the roguelite genre, but it offers a polished and exhilarating experience that rewards bold play and experimentation. For players who enjoy high-octane hack-and-slash combat, cooperative chaos, and the thrill of adapting on the fly, GODBREAKERS stands as a compelling and energetic title that shines brightest when the action is at its most intense. Rating: 7/10

I get it, I am not gonna lie and say good skill cannot overcome a lot of my complaints, but lets see if you can tolerate it till you get good. You have no real time to learn, the game changes constantly and that makes the "skill" excuse hard to overcome. For example, most of the god breaker abilities are different, some are just really bad, slow animation, not well explained etc. Some feel awesome. But you don't get to keep what you like. Its punishing in the worst ways. I'd avoid this game unless you LOVE the trials for Master Rank in Warframe, and you like close but no cigar combat.

I went into God Breakers hoping for a solid experience with RPG elements, but I was completely disappointed by how it handles progression. To be fair, the combat system is genuinely great—it feels fluid and responsive. Unfortunately, that is the game's only redeeming quality. Instead of building your character over time, the game plays like an unforgiving arcade simulator. Whenever you die, all your progression is wiped and you are reset back to the world. You are essentially forced to play through the entire game in a single run without making a mistake. There are little to no RPG elements to make your time investment feel rewarded. If you are looking for a brutal permadeath arcade game, you might like this. But if you want any sense of permanent progression or RPG mechanics, skip it. The combat alone isn't enough to carry the experience. Option 2: Detailed Breakdown (Best for Reddit, Metacritic, or a Blog) The Good: The Combat System: I have to give credit where it's due—the combat is fantastic. It’s well-designed, engaging, and genuinely fun to play. If the rest of the game were built around this combat differently, it would be a hit. The Bad: Zero Meaningful Progression: This was the dealbreaker for me. Any progress you make gets entirely reset upon death, sending you right back to the world. Forced Arcade Mechanics: Rather than a modern RPG, it operates like a coin-op arcade simulator. The game demands that you play through the entire campaign perfectly without dying. Missing RPG Elements: I picked this up expecting RPG mechanics, but they are virtually non-existent. There is no permanent character building or satisfying stat progression to keep you motivated after a loss.
